name: macaque
about: A long-tailed macaque (khỉ đuôi dài, Macaca fascicularis): a male about 50 cm long without the tail, a tail longer than the body, a gray-brown coat with a lighter belly, a bare pink-brown face with pale upper lids, dark hands and feet. It walks on four limbs.
sources: Macaca fascicularis: 38 to 55 cm long without the tail, a tail of 40 to 65 cm; a male 5 to 9 kg, a female 3 to 4 kg; the coat gray-brown to red-brown, the belly lighter (Wikipedia, Crab-eating macaque).
Primates walk on four limbs in the order hind left, front right, hind right, front left (diagonal sequence). The time of a step and the stride are a guess.

The shape, the stance, the sit, the tail and the colors from photos, side by side with renders: https://www.inaturalist.org/photos/178920422 (walk, Fábio Olmos, CC BY), https://www.inaturalist.org/photos/676657297 (stand, Óscar Sampedro, CC BY), https://www.inaturalist.org/photos/310110541 (stand, Lawrence Hylton, CC BY), https://www.inaturalist.org/photos/255353023 (sit, CC0), https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Macaca_fascicularis_Ao_Nang_5.jpg (sit), https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Long-tailed_macaque_(Macaca_fascicularis)_male_head_Angkor.jpg (face).
The lengths of the fur (fur): a guess from photos of the animal, not a measurement.

The template of primates is the mesh of a rhesus macaque of BigMaQ: on it the arms (the upper arm and the forearm) are 0.88 of the legs (the thigh and the shin), and the tail is 0.47 of the head and the body (measured on the mesh).

Wikipedia, Intermembral index (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intermembral_index): the arms over the legs, times 100: 93 for Macaca fascicularis, so the arms 93 / 88 = 1.06 of the template (arm_length 1.06). The tail of the species is as long as the body or longer: tail_length 2.0, the most of the number (0.94 of the body). The narrower body and the thinner limbs and tail: a guess from photos.
